confirmed.title: DemoUi texture and style caches build string keys with Color.ToString and enum ToString on every OnGUI event
confirmed.problem: Every lookup into the runtime texture and style caches builds a new string key. BoxStyle (line 256) uses radius + "|" + fill + "|" + border, Rounded/Disc (line 69) uses "r" + radius + fill + border + borderWidth, Ring (line 95) uses "ring" + radius + thickness + color, and Icon (line 122) uses "icon" + icon. Each Color.ToString() is an F3 format: 4 float strings, an object[] and the result, about 250 B. One Box or Disc key is about 15 allocations and 0.7 KB. These run on every IMGUI event, Layout included, not only Repaint, because Box builds its style before checking the event type and GUI.DrawTexture(..., DemoUi.Icon(..)) evaluates its argument on every event. On the default desktop HUD each event makes 2 Box keys (hotbar frame and prompt pill) and 9 Icon keys (boxing plus concat). Each toast adds 2 more Box keys, the live view 1, and mouse-look adds 2 Ring keys and 1 Disc key. The drawer adds a Disc key per placed-tool row, per map glyph (2 per tool) and per legend entry (9). DemoLauncher's OnGUI uses the same paths.
confirmed.risk: Low. Exact Color equality replaces the old F3-rounded string match. Every caller passes constant colours (static readonly fields, literals, or WithAlpha with constant alpha), so the same entries are reused and the cache stays bounded. The cached != null guards stay for destroyed textures. Needs C# 7 tuples, which the code already uses (DemoLauncher.Known).

votes.reason:
The allocations are real, but "high" overstates the impact. It is closer to low-medium, especially for the VR target.

Confirmed from the code:
- In DemoUi.Box (DemoUi.cs:247-251), BoxStyle(...) is called before the `Event.current.type == EventType.Repaint` check. BoxStyle builds `radius + "|" + fill + "|" + border` (line 256) every time. That is string.Concat(object[]) with a boxed int, two boxed Colors and two Color.ToString() calls (F3 format: four float strings, an object[] and the result), so roughly 0.6-0.8 KB per call.
- `GUI.DrawTexture(..., DemoUi.Icon(...))` evaluates its argument on every event. `"icon" + icon` boxes the enum and concatenates a string.
- Disc and Ring go through Rounded and Ring with the same kind of string keys.
- DemoDesktopPanel has an OnGUI, and DemoToolsBuilder.Create adds the panel to the night store (NightStoreBuilder:164). With GUILayout in use there are at least two events per frame (Layout and Repaint).
- On the default desktop HUD, DrawPrompt does 1 Box, DrawHotbar does 1 Box plus 9 Icon calls, the viewfinder adds 1 Box, and each toast adds 2. That is about 2.5-3 KB per event, so roughly 5-6 KB per frame.
- Nothing in Prototype/Editor references DemoUi, so no validator depends on these caches.

Where the finding overstates:
1. On the main target (PC VR), DesktopActive is false, so the hotbar, prompt pill and crosshair are never drawn. Only the viewfinder Box (1 key) and 2 Box keys per toast remain. That is about 1-2 KB per frame, around 100-150 KB/s at 72-90 Hz. Incremental GC (the Unity 6 default) handles that easily.
2. DemoLauncher's OnGUI calls Box only when there are no map entries (an error state). Its Rounded calls run once in BuildStyles. So the launcher does not "use the same paths" every frame.
3. The same OnGUI makes about as much other garbage on every event. DrawHints and HintWidth call Split and create a new GUIContent for each key and action. ContextPrompt() calls pairs.ToArray(). Chip text is concatenated and gets a new GUIContent. DrawHud builds `new[]{...}` hint arrays. The drawer calls GetComponentsInChildren on every event. So this fix removes only about half of the HUD's per-frame garbage, and the HUD is still not allocation-free.

The proposed fix is safe:
- Color implements IEquatable<Color>, so ValueTuple keys go through EqualityComparer<Color>.Default without boxing.
- Every caller passes constant colours: static palette fields, literals, WithAlpha with a constant alpha, KindColor, ToneColor. The caches stay bounded.
- Box draws only on Repaint today and takes no part in layout, so returning early on other events changes nothing visible.
- The Icon array index is safe: UiIcon has 9 values and IconFor maps DemoToolKind 0-5.
- As a side effect it removes a latent key collision in the current string keys, e.g. Ring(16,5) and Ring(1,65) both produce "ring165...".

It is cheap and touches one file, so it is worth doing as a cleanup, but it should be rated low-medium rather than high.
votes.betterFix:
Apply the proposed tuple-key and Icon-array caches and the Repaint-only early return in DemoUi.Box. To actually make the HUD close to allocation-free, also fix the other per-event garbage in the same OnGUI, otherwise the GC rate only halves:
- DemoUi.DrawHints and HintWidth: reuse one static GUIContent (or GUIContent.Temp-style reuse) instead of `new GUIContent` for each key and action, and avoid `Split('/')` when the string contains no '/'.
- DemoDesktopPanel: cache the constant hint arrays in DrawHud and DrawChips as static readonly fields; have ContextPrompt fill and return a reused list or array instead of `pairs.ToArray()` on every event; rebuild the chip strings only when deployed, NextMarkerNumber or PhotoCount change.
- Skip the drawer's GetComponentsInChildren outside Layout and Repaint, or cache its result on ToolsChanged.

Rate the finding low-medium, because the main VR path only hits the viewfinder and toast Box keys.

votes.reason:
The finding is real. In DemoUi.cs, BoxStyle (line 256), Rounded (line 69), Ring (line 95) and Icon (line 122) all build a string key on every call. Color.ToString() formats four boxed floats with F3, and "icon" + icon boxes the enum. These calls run on every IMGUI event, not only on Repaint. Box (line 247) calls BoxStyle before it checks the event type, and GUI.DrawTexture(..., DemoUi.Icon/Disc/Ring(...)) evaluates its argument on every event. Callers: DemoDesktopPanel lines 287-290, 357, 394, 409, 460, 491-493, 507, 537, 579, 678, 720, 770, 790, 841, 854, and DemoLauncher line 94.

The fix is correct and compiles:
- Unity 6 uses C# 9 / .NET Standard 2.1, so ValueTuple is available, and DemoLauncher.Known already uses tuples.
- UnityEngine.Color implements IEquatable<Color>, and its GetHashCode goes through Vector4.GetHashCode without allocating. ValueTuple's Equals and GetHashCode use EqualityComparer<T>.Default, so a lookup neither boxes nor allocates on Mono or IL2CPP.

The cache stays bounded. I checked every caller of Rounded, Disc, Ring, Icon and Box in Prototype/Scripts:
- Each passes a constant colour: palette static readonly fields, literals, Color.white, WithAlpha with a constant alpha, Color.Lerp of constants in Build(), or DemoFeedback.ToneColor, which returns palette constants.
- Toast fades go through GUI.color, not through the cache key.
- So keying on the exact colour value never creates new entries per frame.
- Exact matching is slightly more correct than the F3-rounded strings. It also removes a latent string collision, for example Ring(16,5) and Ring(1,65) both making the key "ring165...".

The Box change only moves the BoxStyle lookup after the existing Repaint check, because style.Draw already ran only on Repaint. Textures are now built on the first Repaint instead of the first Layout event, which changes nothing visible. Box uses explicit Rects, not GUILayout, so skipping it on Layout events does not change the layout.

No validator is affected:
- No Editor or validator code uses DemoUi.textures, boxes, Rounded, Ring, Icon or Box, by name or by reflection. DemoValidation only looks up DemoUiTheme.
- No validator reads DemoUi.cs as source text.
- ShopCityValidation says OnGUI never runs in batch mode.

Worth it: the change rewrites about 15 lines and does not add complexity. It removes roughly 0.7 KB per Box or Disc key and about 50 B per Icon key, on every event, every frame.

I would rate the impact medium rather than high, for two reasons:
- In VR, DemoDesktopPanel draws only the strip (two Box calls) and the toasts, not the hotbar or crosshair.
- OnGUI still allocates in other places: new GUIContent, Split('/') in HintWidth and DrawHints, the chip and strip string concatenations, and new[] {...} hint arrays in DrawHud. This fix removes only part of the per-event garbage.
votes.betterFix:
Apply the fix as proposed, with three small refinements:
(1) Size the icon cache as `new Texture2D[(int)UiIcon.UVTorch + 1]` (or keep Enum.GetValues; it runs once either way). For an out-of-range icon, fall back to building the texture without caching it, so a stray cast cannot index outside the array.
(2) Keep the `cached != null` / `style.normal.background != null` guards.
(3) Put the Repaint early-return at the top of Box: `if (Event.current.type != EventType.Repaint) return;`.

To get the rest of the GC win later, cache the per-event allocations in DemoDesktopPanel and DemoUi that this fix leaves:
- Precompute the split key arrays for the constant hint pairs instead of calling Split('/') in HintWidth and DrawHints.
- Hoist the `new[] { "P", "Photo", ... }` arrays in DrawHud into static readonly fields.
- Reuse one GUIContent for CalcSize.
That is a separate change from this finding.

confirmed.title: VR controller tooltips keep about 55 transparent renderers drawing after they fade to alpha 0
confirmed.problem: ApplyTipAlpha only writes colours. It never disables renderers, so the faded-out hints keep rendering. ShowHints is the only code that changes `enabled`, and only on the menu button. After the 20 s onboarding, when the controller is not looked at, tipAlpha is 0, but every tip still renders 5 transparent objects: the panel and key-panel MeshRenderers, two TextMesh renderers and a LineRenderer. That is 6 tips on the left and 5 on the right, 55 renderers with mostly unique runtime materials (3 per tip), so they do not batch. They are culled, sorted back to front and drawn every frame while VR is active and the hands are in view, fully transparent. The status card does this correctly (ApplyStatusAlpha disables its renderers at alpha 0). There is also related waste: every button press or release forces ApplyTipAlpha (line 482, `if (hintsShown) appliedTipAlpha = -1;`) even when the hints are invisible. That rewrites 12 TextMesh colours, which rebuilds 12 text meshes, and 18 material colours per press.
confirmed.risk: Low. DemoValidation.InterfaceChecks checks TooltipCount, Model and StatusText, and invokes LateUpdate by reflection, so the method name and signature must stay. None of it reads the tooltip renderers' enabled state. The A/X Label TextMesh from the builder becomes tip.Action, so its renderer is cached too. XRControllerInput.ApplyHints only touches the Label renderer when hud is null, so there is no conflict.

votes.reason:
I could not refute it. The code works as the finding describes.

What the code does:
- ApplyTipAlpha (XRHandHud.cs:287-299) only writes colours. The only code that changes `enabled` on tip renderers is ShowHints (277-285).
- After onboarding, when the controller is not looked at, tipTarget is 0. MoveTowards lands exactly on 0, so line 487 calls ApplyTipAlpha(0), and every renderer stays enabled.

The count is right:
- The left hand has 6 tips (Menu is left only) and the right hand has 5.
- Each tip has 5 renderers: the Panel and KeyPanel MeshRenderers, two TextMesh renderers and a LineRenderer. That makes 55.
- DemoUi.WorldPanel calls UnlitMaterial, which does `new Material` for each panel, and each line gets its own material. That gives 3 unique materials per tip. The text renderers share one CrimeScene/WorldText material per font. Built-in renders alpha-0 transparent objects anyway (Sprites/Default and TextMesh have no alpha cull), so they are culled, sorted and drawn.
- The XR hands are only active in VR mode, so the cost is VR-only, as stated.

One effect the finding missed makes it a little worse. Line positions are updated only while tipAlpha > 0, and the LineRenderers use world space. When the hints fade out, the invisible lines stay where they were in the world and can still be drawn when that spot is in view, even if the hands are not.

The impact is somewhat overstated. Tips at alpha 0 only reach the screen when the hands are in the periphery: in the field of view but more than 30 degrees from the gaze, or more than 0.8 m away. Out of view they are culled, except for the stale lines. In that case the cost is roughly 55 draw calls and around 30 SetPass calls on the render thread, a few tenths of a ms at 90 Hz. That is low-to-medium rather than medium. GPU fill is negligible.

The button-press part is real but trivial. Line 482 does force a re-apply at alpha 0, which writes 12 text colours on the left hand (10 on the right) plus the panel and line colours. That happens at human press rate, not per frame.

The fix is still worth it. It is small, local, and copies the existing ApplyStatusAlpha pattern.

The fix is safe. When alpha goes from 0 back above 0, ApplyTipAlpha re-enables the renderers, and lines 489-495 update the line positions in the same LateUpdate, before rendering. The risk note has one gap: it says no validator reads the tooltip renderers' enabled state. ShopCityValidation.cs:185-189 ("Hand hints toggle together") does read `Label.GetComponent<Renderer>().enabled`, and the Label is tip.Action. That check still passes with the proposed fix:
- ShowHints sets the renderers directly from `visible`.
- The check runs in LocomotionChecks with no frame in between.
- The only reflective LateUpdate call is in DemoValidation.InterfaceChecks, which runs after it in the stage-1 order (ShopCityValidation.cs:97-104).

The fix should keep toggling renderer.enabled rather than calling SetActive on tip.Root. With SetActive, that check could not see the hints hide, because Renderer.enabled stays true on an inactive object.
votes.betterFix: Use the proposed fix as written: cache the KeyRenderer and ActionRenderer, add SetTipRenderers, gate ApplyTipAlpha on `hintsShown && alpha > 0.001f`, and gate line 482 on `tipAlpha > 0`. Optionally, call SetTipRenderers only when the visible state actually changes (store a bool on the HUD), so the renderers are not toggled on every ApplyTipAlpha call during a fade. Correct the risk note to say that ShopCityValidation "Hand hints toggle together" reads the A/X Label renderer's enabled flag and still passes, because ShowHints sets it directly. Do not use SetActive on tip.Root.

votes.reason:
The finding is real. In Prototype/Scripts/XRHandHud.cs, ApplyTipAlpha (lines 287-299) only writes colours. The only code that toggles `enabled` on the tip renderers is ShowHints (277-285). So when hints are on but the controller is not looked at, each tip still draws 5 renderers at alpha 0: Panel, KeyPanel, Key, Action/Label and the Leader line. That is 6 tips on the left and 5 on the right. DemoUi.WorldPanel creates its own UnlitMaterial for every call, and every Leader gets its own unlit material, so each tip has 3 unique materials and they cannot batch. The status card already does the right thing: ApplyStatusAlpha turns its renderers off at alpha 0.

The waste only happens when a controller is in the frustum but outside the 30 degree look cone. That is common in VR, so the cost is real but modest: roughly 33 SetPass calls and up to 55 draws of render-thread CPU, and almost nothing on the GPU. I would call it low-medium rather than medium. Two small errors in the finding: a button press rewrites 12 TextMesh colours on the left hand and 10 on the right, and LineRenderer colours are vertex colours, not material colours. Neither changes the verdict.

Correctness and compilation: it uses only Renderer.enabled, chained bool property assignment (already used in this file) and a private static helper on the private nested Tip class. That compiles on Unity 6000 Built-in with no packages.

Runtime: ShowHints(true) turns renderers on and sets appliedTipAlpha to -1. Every caller runs from Update (XRControllerInput menu press, then ToggleHints) or from a validator, so this frame's LateUpdate sees the -1, re-applies the alpha and either writes fresh colours or turns the renderers off again before rendering. That means no frame shows a pop or stale colours. A hand that is inactive at the time gets fixed on its first LateUpdate.

The line 482 change, `hintsShown && tipAlpha > 0`, is also correct. If the hints start fading in on the same frame, the |tipAlpha - appliedTipAlpha| > 0.02 test re-applies them anyway, and the existing exact-0/exact-1 clause at 487 guarantees the renderers switch off at 0. At 72-90 Hz each fade step is 0.055-0.07, so the hints fade in without delay.

Validators: the only check that reads tip renderer state is ShopCityValidation.LocomotionChecks, "Hand hints toggle together", lines 184-190. It reads Label.GetComponent<Renderer>().enabled right after mode.Apply(true) and after two ToggleHints calls, all inside one synchronous Tick in play mode, and no LateUpdate runs in between.

- `shown` still passes. Renderers are on by default after Build. Awake calls ShowHints(true). DemoModeSwitch.Start makes the hands inactive from the first frame, so any LateUpdate before Tick stage 1 (frameCount >= 10) runs during the 20 s onboarding with alpha 1.
- `hidden` and `restored` pass, because ShowHints itself still switches the renderers synchronously. Forcing them on in ShowHints(true) is exactly what this check needs. Letting LateUpdate enable them instead would fail it.

ShopCity runs LocomotionChecks before DemoValidation.InterfaceChecks. InterfaceChecks only reads TooltipCount, Model, StatusText, the carousel and Label.text, and calls LateUpdate by reflection, whose name and signature stay the same. NightStoreValidation only calls InterfaceChecks. StoreKitValidation and DemoValidation's ToolStage, PhotoStage and ResetStage never touch the tip renderers. XRControllerInput.ApplyHints writes the Label renderer only when hud is null, so nothing conflicts. The builder's Label becomes tip.Action and is cached as ActionRenderer, so it is covered.

It costs about 12 lines, follows the existing status-card pattern, and has low risk.

confirmed.title: Overview map re-renders the whole store 4 times a second whenever the drawer is open, on every tab, with the shadow pass
confirmed.problem: ShouldRender (line 20) is true for PanelLayout.Full whatever the tab, but the map texture is drawn only by MapTab. The drawer opens on the Tools tab by default and presenters keep it open to spawn tools, reset and switch the scene. Meanwhile Update calls overview.Render() every 0.25 s. That render is synchronous on the main thread: culling plus draw submission for every renderer in the 2*HalfSize square (the night store budget allows 900 renderers), with occlusion culling off. It also renders shadow maps for this camera. In the daytime shop (Standalone default quality Ultra: soft shadows, 150 m) that means the sun's cascades every time. In the night store NightQuality's 14 m shadow distance mostly culls them for a camera 20 m up. In VR that is a periodic frame-time spike about every 22nd frame at 90 Hz for a texture nobody sees.
confirmed.risk: Low for the tab gate. MapChecks and BackdropChecks call map.Render() directly and only test map.Texture != null and UV mapping. For the shadow change, check once in the Frame Debugger that shadowDistance = 0 suppresses the shadow passes in the Built-in pipeline. If not, use QualitySettings.shadows = ShadowQuality.Disable with the same save and restore. Both are restored synchronously in finally, so NightQuality's saved values are unaffected.

votes.reason:
The core waste is confirmed. DemoOverviewMap.ShouldRender (line 20) checks only panel.isActiveAndEnabled and Layout == Full. Update (lines 46-51) calls overview.Render() every 0.25 s, synchronously on the main thread, with occlusion culling off (line 42). Map.Texture is drawn in exactly one place, DemoDesktopPanel.MapTab (line 792); nothing else reads it. Tab is restored from PlayerPrefs and defaults to Tools.

DemoModeSwitch never disables the panel, so it stays active in VR mode. In VR, SpawnFromPanel leaves the drawer open, so a presenter can keep it open on the Tools, Camera, Scene or Settings tab for long stretches. All that time the store is re-rendered 4 times a second into a texture nobody sees. The time arithmetic is right: 0.25 s is about every 22nd frame at 90 Hz.

Parts of the impact claim are overstated or wrong:
(1) "In the daytime shop that means the sun's cascades every time" is false. In the Glass chain, ShopInteriorFinish.ApplyShell calls ConfigureLighting, which sets shadows = None on every light, sun included. CheckBudget even asserts "Lighting uses at most four shadowless lights". DemoValidation's PreviewSun is added with AddComponent, which leaves shadows at None. The night store's sun (DiagnosticSun) is also shadowless, and the moon, streetlights and headlights are baked. The only realtime shadow casters in either scene are the flashlight spot (Hard, Low resolution) and the lamp tools.
(2) The 900 figure is the renderer budget, not a measured count. The daytime shop measures about 323 mesh renderers and 14k triangles.
So the extra cost is mainly one more cull and a few hundred draw submissions at 256x256, plus possibly a low-resolution spot shadow map when the flashlight or a lamp is on. That is low to medium, not a cascade-driven spike.

There is also a minor inaccuracy: the tab-switch click is processed in a MouseUp event, and the Repaint that follows in the same frame already draws the Map tab, so the old or uninitialized texture can show for one frame. This is harmless.

The tab gate in Update is a trivial, safe change. It leaves ShouldRender alone, so ShopRobberyDressing's two checks, which only set panel.Visible, still pass. MapChecks and BackdropChecks call map.Render() directly and are unaffected.
votes.betterFix:
Apply only the tab gate in Update: `if (!ShouldRender || panel.Tab != PanelTab.Map || Time.unscaledTime < nextRender) return;`. Keep ShouldRender and Render() unchanged.

Drop the save-and-restore of QualitySettings.shadowDistance around overview.Render(). Its premise, the sun's shadow cascades, does not exist in either scene: the daytime sun is forced shadowless and the night lights are baked. At most it would skip a low-resolution flashlight or lamp spot shadow map, and it puts a global QualitySettings write on the render path for no measurable gain.

Add the proposed validator check: with panel.Visible = true and panel.Tab = PanelTab.Tools, invoke Update by reflection and confirm that no render happened (for example, nextRender did not advance). Set panel.Tab explicitly in the check, because Tab comes from PlayerPrefs.

votes.reason:
I confirmed the problem in the code. DemoOverviewMap.ShouldRender (line 20) checks only Layout == Full. Map.Texture is used in one place, DemoDesktopPanel.MapTab (line 792). Nothing else references DemoOverviewMap.Texture. So every 0.25 s the store is rendered synchronously into a texture that only one tab shows. In the night store, DemoDesktopPanel.Tab defaults to Tools, or whatever tab PlayerPrefs saved.

The proposed fix compiles against Unity 6000 Built-in with no packages. PanelTab and panel.Tab are public, `!ShouldRender ||` short-circuits before panel is dereferenced, and QualitySettings.shadowDistance is a plain float property. Every existing validator check still passes. ShopRobberyDressing's two checks use ShouldRender, which is unchanged. MapChecks (NightStoreValidation:990) and BackdropChecks (ShopCityValidation:545) call map.Render() directly and only test that Texture != null and the UV mapping. NightQuality.Restore and the "Night quality settings applied" check are unaffected, because the shadow distance is put back synchronously in finally.

Timing still works. DemoDesktopPanel has execution order -200, so a Tab key press sets Layout before the map's Update in the same frame. Leaving the Map tab leaves nextRender in the past, so returning to it renders on the next Update.

The tab gate is clearly worth one condition. A synchronous 256 px render of up to 900 renderers every 22nd frame at 90 Hz is a real VR spike, and the drawer stays open on the Tools tab for long periods. The shadow suppression saves little in the night store. There only the flashlight casts realtime shadows (NightStoreValidation:546-553), and at 18 m+ from the camera it is beyond the 14 m shadow distance. In the daytime shop it skips the sun's cascades and the screen-space shadow collect. Zeroing QualitySettings.shadowDistance around a manual Render is the usual Built-in trick to turn shadows off for one camera. If it does nothing, it costs nothing.

Two flaws in the plan:
(1) The proposed validator check cannot be written as described. Validators run in edit mode through -executeMethod. No frames advance there, and nothing records a render count, so "advance a frame or call Update by reflection and confirm no render" can only be done by reading the private nextRender field by reflection, which is brittle.
(2) "The tab never shows a stale image" is not quite right. GUILayout.Button fires on the MouseUp OnGUI pass, and the deferred SelectTab runs at the end of that pass. The Repaint pass in the same frame then draws MapTab before the next Update renders. That shows one frame of the last map image, or an RT that has not been rendered yet on the first visit. It does no harm but should not be claimed.

confirmed.title: Photo capture: synchronous GPU readback, a needless 8 MB texture upload and a fresh 6 MB array per photo
confirmed.problem: ReadPixels (lines 276-292) does three expensive things on the main thread in the shutter frame. (1) scratch.ReadPixels forces a CPU-GPU sync on the 1920x1080 target, so the main thread waits for the render thread and GPU to drain. (2) scratch.Apply(false) (line 288) uploads the whole 1920x1080 RGB24 scratch to the GPU (converted to RGBA, about 8 MB), although scratch is never rendered and only its CPU bytes are read. (3) scratch.GetRawTextureData() (line 289) allocates a new 6.2 MB managed byte[] for every photo. The same frame then uploads LastPhoto again (lines 257-258), and the review recorder copies files (CPU-GC-7). The result is a multi-millisecond hitch exactly when the visitor presses the shutter in the headset, and repeated 6 MB managed allocations that grow the Boehm heap and lengthen every later GC mark.
confirmed.risk: Step 1: low. ReadPixels fills the CPU copy and Apply only affects the GPU copy. LastPhoto still gets its own LoadRawTextureData + Apply, so PhotoFrame, CameraScreen and the panel are unchanged, and DemoValidation.PhotoStage (file exists, PhotoCount, frame width 1920, camera pose restored) still passes. Step 2: medium. It adds 2-3 frames of capture latency, which PhotoStage's 30 s wait tolerates. Check the image orientation and the RGBA32-to-RGB24 conversion against Docs/Verification runtime-photo.png. ShopCityValidation's viewfinder check (photo.targetTexture == null && !photo.enabled) needs the camera restored before the first yield.

votes.reason:
Mostly confirmed from the code, but the impact is overstated.

What holds up, in Prototype/Scripts/EvidenceCamera.cs:
- ReadPixels (lines 276-292) runs on the main thread in the coroutine step right after the photo camera rendered. Texture2D.ReadPixels from a RenderTexture is a synchronous readback that flushes the render thread and GPU.
- scratch.Apply(false) on line 288 is pure waste. The scratch texture is only referenced inside this file (grep finds no other use; LastPhoto is a separate texture with its own LoadRawTextureData + Apply). ReadPixels fills the CPU copy, and GetRawTextureData() reads the CPU copy, so the 1920x1080 RGB24 upload (padded to RGBA on D3D11, about 8 MB) is never used.
- The non-generic GetRawTextureData() on line 289 returns a new managed byte[] of 1920*1080*3 = 6,220,800 bytes on every photo.

What is overstated or wrong:
1. This is not a per-frame hot path. It runs once per shutter press, maybe a handful to a few dozen times a session. "Medium" is generous; low-to-medium is fairer.
2. The biggest shutter-frame costs stay: the extra full 1920x1080 scene render of the photo camera, and the synchronous readback stall. Step 1 removes only the Apply (roughly 1-3 ms of conversion and upload) and the 6 MB allocation, not the stall.
3. "Lengthen every later GC mark" is wrong. Mono/Boehm allocates byte[] pointer-free (atomic), so these arrays are never scanned. The real GC effect is heap growth plus a chance that a 6 MB allocation triggers a collection at some point.
4. "The same frame then uploads LastPhoto again" is wrong. Lines 257-258 run only after the PNG save task finishes (about 100 ms, several frames later), not in the shutter frame.

Safety of Step 1:
- Removing Apply cannot change any CPU bytes, the PNG, LastPhoto, PhotoFrame, CameraScreen, the panel, or DemoValidation.PhotoStage.
- Reusing the buffer is also safe. The coroutine sets IsCapturing=false at line 248 and calls LoadRawTextureData at line 257 with no yield in between, and CapturePhoto is blocked while IsCapturing is true.
- The one race is the one the finding names: OnDisable calls StopAllCoroutines and Restore, which clears IsCapturing while the Task.Run PNG encode may still be reading `pixels`. Nulling the buffer in OnDisable handles it.
- Unity.Collections.NativeArray and GetRawTextureData<T> are in the core module, so nothing conflicts with the no-packages rule.

Step 2 (AsyncGPUReadback) is a real redesign. RestoreCamera has to be split, there are 2-3 frames of extra latency, and RGB24 conversion support needs checking. It is optional and not risk-free.

Overall the change is worth doing because it is tiny and removes clearly wasted work, but it will not remove the shutter hitch.
votes.betterFix:
Minimal and risk-free: delete line 288 (`scratch.Apply(false);`) and change the comment on line 275 to say the CPU copy is all that is read. That is the clearly wasted work, and it changes no bytes.

If you also want to cut the 6 MB allocation per photo, keep a `private byte[] pixelBuffer`. Fill it with `NativeArray<byte> raw = scratch.GetRawTextureData<byte>(); if (pixelBuffer == null || pixelBuffer.Length != raw.Length) pixelBuffer = new byte[raw.Length]; raw.CopyTo(pixelBuffer); return pixelBuffer;` and set `pixelBuffer = null` in OnDisable. An in-flight Task.Run encode then keeps its own array if the component is disabled mid-save.

Leave AsyncGPUReadback for a separate, Unity-verified change. It is the only fix that removes the actual stall, but it needs RestoreCamera split: restore the camera before the first yield, release the temporary RT after the request completes. Also check the RGB24 conversion and orientation against Docs/Verification runtime-photo.png.

After the change, rerun DemoValidation PhotoStage and NightStoreValidation.RunNightQuick, and mark the change unverified in HANDOFF.md until those have run.

votes.reason:
Checked against /home/user/Jewelry-store-vr-demo/Prototype/Scripts/EvidenceCamera.cs (lines 195-292, 333-344) and the validators. The problem is real. `scratch` is private and only its CPU bytes are read through GetRawTextureData. Texture2D.ReadPixels fills the CPU copy, and Apply only uploads it to the GPU. On D3D11, which has no RGB24 format, that upload also converts on the CPU to RGBA32, about 8.3 MB. So `scratch.Apply(false)` costs main-thread time and bandwidth for nothing. `GetRawTextureData()` also allocates a fresh 6.2 MB byte[] for every photo.

Step 1 compiles on Unity 6000 Built-in with no packages. NativeArray<T> and Texture2D.GetRawTextureData<T>() are in UnityEngine.CoreModule under the Unity.Collections namespace, and NativeArray.CopyTo(T[]) works because the buffer is sized to raw.Length. The CPU data is identical to before, so EncodeArrayToPNG, LastPhoto.LoadRawTextureData/Apply, PhotoFrame, CameraScreen and the panel are unchanged.

Reusing the buffer is sound. The Task closure and LoadRawTextureData both read `pixels`. IsCapturing becomes false on line 248 in the same coroutine step as the LoadRawTextureData on line 257, with no yield in between. Capture() always yields before ReadPixels, so even a capture started from CaptureFailed or PhotoSaved cannot overwrite the buffer early. The only hazard is OnDisable: StopAllCoroutines plus Restore clears IsCapturing while the save task may still be encoding. Setting `pixelBuffer = null` in OnDisable covers that.

All validator checks still pass:
- DemoValidation.PhotoStage: file exists, PhotoCount == 1, PhotoFrame.Current.width == 1920, PhotoCamera local pose restored.
- ResetStage.
- NightStoreValidation.
- ShopCityValidation's viewfinder check (targetTexture == null && !enabled).
No validator reads EvidenceCamera's source text or private fields.

Two parts of the finding are overstated:
- The LastPhoto upload is not in the shutter frame. It runs after the save task, about 100 ms later.
- The main cost Step 1 removes is the Apply, so the hitch shrinks but the ReadPixels sync stall stays.

Step 2 (AsyncGPUReadback) should not ship blind:
- Requesting TextureFormat.RGB24 needs conversion to a 3-byte format that GPUs do not support natively, and support for that varies by platform and version.
- Row order can differ from ReadPixels.
- RestoreCamera would have to be split, and OnDisable would then release the RT while a request may still be pending.
- None of this can be checked here, and the gain is about one GPU-sync frame at a single shutter press, which ASW over Link hides.

Step 1 is about 6 lines and clearly worth it. Step 2 is not worth it until it can be tested on the PC.
votes.betterFix:
Do only Step 1 now.

1. In ReadPixels, delete `scratch.Apply(false);`.
2. Replace `return scratch.GetRawTextureData();` with:
```csharp
var raw = scratch.GetRawTextureData<byte>(); // NativeArray view of the CPU copy, no allocation
if (pixelBuffer == null || pixelBuffer.Length != raw.Length) pixelBuffer = new byte[raw.Length];
raw.CopyTo(pixelBuffer);
return pixelBuffer;
```
Using `var`, or `Unity.Collections.NativeArray<byte>` written out in full, avoids adding a using directive.
3. Add the field `private byte[] pixelBuffer; // reused; IsCapturing guards it until LoadRawTextureData has run`.
4. Add `pixelBuffer = null;` to OnDisable after Restore(), so a save task that is still running keeps its own array.
5. Update the comment on line 275, which says ReadPixels returns a copy.

Add the check that CLAUDE.md requires to DemoValidation.PhotoStage, for example comparing `evidence.LastPhoto.GetPixel(960, 540)` with the decoded runtime-photo.png. That proves the CPU bytes still match without Apply. Mark it unverified until the user runs NightStoreValidation.RunNightQuick and ShopCityValidation.RunGlass.

If the shutter stall is ever measured as a problem, put AsyncGPUReadback behind `SystemInfo.supportsAsyncGPUReadback` and keep ReadPixels as the fallback:
- Request TextureFormat.RGBA32, not RGB24.
- Strip the alpha to RGB inside the existing Task.Run, off the main thread, so the PNG stays opaque and there is no GPU format conversion.
- Restore the camera before the first yield, and release the temporary RT only after `request.done`, in OnDisable too.
- Check the image orientation against Docs/Verification/runtime-photo.png on the PC before relying on it.

confirmed.title: HUD allocates GUIContent, split arrays, hint arrays and strings on every OnGUI event
confirmed.problem: Apart from CPU-GC-1, the always-on HUD makes dozens of small allocations per event, with at least 2 events per frame (Layout + Repaint). (a) New hint arrays at every call site: lines 233, 258 and 618, help line 1025, DemoLauncher line 115. (b) ContextPrompt (309-336) allocates a params array through Add(params string[]) plus pairs.ToArray() every event, then DemoUi.HintWidth and DrawHints (DemoUi.cs 405-435) each run pairs[i].Split('/') and new GUIContent(...) twice per pair. (c) Chip, StripChip, StripButton, DrawCrosshair, DrawPointerTip, DrawPrompt and DrawToasts each call new GUIContent(text) (lines 263, 293, 303, 362, 484, 563, 571), and DrawResetBanner (503) allocates its constant GUIContent. (d) Chip and status strings are concatenated every event (lines 247-249, 553-555, 637-638), and hotbar counts use kindCounts[i].ToString() (414). (e) The drawer tabs call tab.ToString() 5 times per event (601). (f) DeployedTool.Title (DeployedTool.cs line 49) allocates 3 objects (char string, Substring, concat) and DisplayName (line 55) concatenates. Both run per event through TargetName while hovering, ToolTile ×6 and the placed rows. (g) With useGUILayout left true, Unity sends a Layout pass before every event, although only the drawer and the controls overlay use GUILayout.
confirmed.risk: Low for (a)-(f). The strings and order are identical: InterfaceChecks reads ContextPrompt()/ContextMessage() and the carousel check compares against DeployedTool.Title(Marker), and both keep their values. The shared GUIContent is safe because IMGUI is single-threaded and every use finishes before the next Temp call. Medium for (g): any GUILayout call reached while useGUILayout is false logs layout errors. Today the HUD, strip, toasts, banner and flash paths use only GUI.*, and Unity checks useGUILayout per event, so a deferred switch to Full gets its Layout pass on the next event. Verify by opening and closing the drawer and the F1 overlay with the mouse and the keyboard.

The script never sets useGUILayout, so Unity sends a Layout event before Repaint and before every input event. That makes at least 2 OnGUI calls per frame.
- **Desktop, default state** (layout Hidden, HUD and prompts on, nothing hovered, camera present). Each event:

  - DrawPrompt: ContextPrompt uses Add(params) with an 8-element array (line 332), then pairs.ToArray(). HintWidth and DrawHints each Split 4 keys and create 8 GUIContents.
  - DrawHotbar: kindCounts[i].ToString() for each kind with a count.
  - DrawViewfinder: a new hint array (line 233) plus the same Split/GUIContent work.
  - DrawToasts: one GUIContent per toast.

- **Hover and drawer.** TargetName -> DeployedTool.DisplayName/Title allocates per event while hovering a tool. The drawer adds tab.ToString() x5, ToolTile Title x6, the placed rows and StatusLine. DemoLauncher line 115 runs only in the start-menu scene, so it does not matter.

- **The 90 Hz case does the least work.** In PC VR, DesktopActive is false, so DrawPrompt, DrawHotbar, DrawPointerTip and DrawCrosshair never run. Only the chips, two hint rows, the viewfinder hints and the toasts remain, about 20-25 objects per event, roughly 1-2 KB per frame.

Rating: low-to-medium. Still worth doing, because the change is cheap, low-risk hygiene for a VR main thread.

Is the fix safe?
- **(a)-(f): yes.** DemoValidation.cs:237/239 uses Array.IndexOf on ContextPrompt(), which keeps its string[] signature and contents. DemoValidation.cs:270 compares against DeployedTool.Title(Marker), which keeps its value. XRHandHud.cs:359 also calls Title and is unaffected.

- **(g) needs care.** The drawer and overlay can be opened by deferred clicks inside OnGUI: the strip's "Panel" button, Settings "Controls (F1)", and the help-overlay toggle buttons. useGUILayout must therefore be updated by the Layout/HelpOpen setters, not only in Update. Give Layout and HelpOpen backing fields whose setters call SyncLayoutFlag() (`useGUILayout = layout == PanelLayout.Full || helpOpen`), and call it in Awake. A setter covers deferred clicks, external callers and the validators; a check in Update alone would miss a deferred click that opens the drawer inside OnGUI.
2. **Then the cheap static parts.**

   - Add DemoUi.Temp(text) and a key-parts cache (Dictionary<string,string[]>) in HintWidth and DrawHints.
   - Make TabNames a static array, use a precomputed "0".."99" table for counts, and store Title strings in a static array.
   - In ContextPrompt use Add(string,string) overloads, and let DrawPrompt fill and use `pairs` directly while the public ContextPrompt() still returns ToArray() for DemoValidation.
3. **Lowest priority: caching the chip and status strings** on (deployed, NextMarkerNumber, PhotoCount). It adds state for few bytes saved.
4. **Fix DemoUi.BoxStyle's per-call key before or alongside this** (radius + "|" + fill + "|" + border runs Color.ToString() on every Box call). It probably allocates more than everything here combined. A struct key, or a key computed from radius and the colour converted to Color32 and packed into ints, avoids it.
5. **Verify with the Profiler's GC Alloc column** in VR and desktop modes rather than assuming zero.

votes.reason:
Every cited line checks out. Hint arrays are created at lines 233, 258, 618 and 1025 and at DemoLauncher line 115. ContextPrompt allocates a params array plus ToArray. confirmed.title: Drawer re-walks the deployment hierarchy with GetComponentsInChildren on every OnGUI event
confirmed.problem: PlacedTools (line 704, the default Tools tab) and MapTab (line 794) call Station.DeploymentRoot.GetComponentsInChildren<DeployedTool>() on every IMGUI event while the drawer is open. Each call allocates a new array and walks every transform under DeploymentRoot: every tool's geometry, number labels and the tape ribbons, hundreds of transforms in a busy scene. That happens 2-4 times a frame. Line 704 also allocates `new DeployedTool[0]` when the root is missing. Recount (lines 1052-1062) already walks the same hierarchy on every ToolsChanged (spawn, place, remove, clear, tape and lamp changes). Tools stay under DeploymentRoot while held, so the set only changes with that event.
confirmed.risk: Low. Recount is subscribed in OnEnable to Station.ToolsChanged, which ToolStation fires on Spawn, NotifyPlaced, SetLampLit, tape selection, RemoveTool and ClearTools (also used by DemoSession.ResetSession). The null and inactive skip covers the frame between Destroy and the event. No validator inspects the drawer lists.

votes.reason:
The problem is real, but the finding rates it higher than it is. It is low impact, not medium.

Reproduction: when Layout == PanelLayout.Full, OnGUI calls DrawDrawer. The Tools tab is the default; Awake restores the saved tab from PlayerPrefs. Every OnGUI event (at least Layout and Repaint each frame, plus one more pair per input event) then calls PlacedTools, which runs DeploymentRoot.GetComponentsInChildren<DeployedTool>() at line 704. That allocates a new array and walks the whole hierarchy under DeploymentRoot. MapTab at line 794 does the same thing. PlacedTools and MapTab are separate cases of one switch, so only one of them runs per event. "2-4 times a frame" is right when it counts events, not both calls together. OnGUI also runs in VR mode on the desktop mirror, so a presenter who leaves the drawer open does add this cost to the VR frame.

Why the impact is overstated:
- Tools are small. DemoToolGeometry builds each one from about 3-6 transforms (Base, Shell, Band, number label, TapeAnchor and so on). A busy scene of 30 tools is roughly 100-200 transforms, so each walk takes a few microseconds and allocates about N*8+32 bytes.
- The same drawer pass already makes much more garbage in every event:
  - tab.ToString() and a closure display class for each of the 5 tab buttons
  - a closure for each Remove row
  - the StatusLine string concatenation and the per-chip and per-row string concatenations
  - the new[] hint arrays
  - the DemoUi.Disc/Rounded key strings (CPU-GC-1)
  - IMGUI's own GUILayout allocations
- The drawer starts closed (the ShopRobberyDressing validator checks this), and on desktop it captures input while it is open.

So this fix removes only a small part of the drawer's per-event allocation and will not show up in frame time by itself. It is worth doing only because it costs about 10 lines and carries no risk.

Safety, checked against the code:
- The only code that creates tools is ToolStation.Spawn, which fires ToolsChanged.
- Every removal fires ToolsChanged synchronously after SetActive(false): ToolStation.RemoveTool (through DeployedTool.RemoveTool) and ClearTools (also used by DemoSession). ToolHolder.Remove and DesktopInteractor/HandInteractor removals all go through Station.RemoveTool. Recount's walk skips inactive objects, so removed tools drop out immediately.
- Held tools stay under DeploymentRoot. ToolHolder says so, and no script reparents them; the only SetParent calls in the interactors are for the camera.
- Nothing calls SetSiblingIndex, so a cached list keeps the same order as a live walk.
- Station is serialized by DemoToolsBuilder, so OnEnable subscribes Recount and runs it once.
- No validator touches PlacedTools, MapTab or kindCounts. OnGUI does not run in batch mode, and the validators only check Layout, Contains, ContextPrompt and RequestReset.
votes.betterFix:
Fill a `List<DeployedTool> placed` inside Recount, as the finding proposes. Then make three changes:
- In PlacedTools, use `placed.Count` in place of `tools.Length`, both for the "Nothing placed yet" check and for the "+N earlier" and `first` arithmetic. This removes the `new DeployedTool[0]` branch.
- In MapTab, loop over `placed` by index.
- Skip only `tool == null`, as a guard against a scene unload.

Do not filter on `activeInHierarchy` inside the row loop. Every removal path already fires ToolsChanged synchronously after SetActive(false), so the list is never stale between events. Filtering in the loop would also leave the count and "+N earlier" text out of step with the rows actually drawn. If an inactive-root guard is wanted, check `Station.DeploymentRoot.gameObject.activeInHierarchy` once at the top of the method.

Apply this together with the CPU-GC-1 change to DemoUi.Disc and the other per-event allocations in the drawer:
- cache the tab labels instead of calling enum ToString each event
- keep the hint arrays in static readonly fields
- cache StatusLine and rebuild it only when Recount runs

On its own, this finding barely changes the drawer's garbage.

votes.reason:
The finding is accurate, but its impact is overstated. It is closer to low than medium.

What the code does now:
- PlacedTools (DemoDesktopPanel.cs:704) and MapTab (DemoDesktopPanel.cs:794) call GetComponentsInChildren<DeployedTool>() on every IMGUI event while the drawer is open on the Tools tab or the Map tab.
- Line 704 also allocates `new DeployedTool[0]` when the deployment root is missing.

Why the cached list stays correct:
- Tools never change parent. Nothing in Prototype/Scripts calls SetParent on a DeployedTool; ToolHolder moves held tools by position only.
- Tools enter the hierarchy in one place only: ToolStation.Spawn, which instantiates under DeploymentRoot and then fires ToolsChanged.
- Tools leave it in two places, ToolStation.RemoveTool and ClearTools. Both deactivate the object, then Destroy it, then fire ToolsChanged in the same call. ToolHolder.Remove, DesktopInteractor.Remove and DemoSession.ResetSession all go through these.
- Recount uses the default includeInactive=false, so it already drops a tool that is deactivated but not yet destroyed.
- Recount runs in OnEnable, so the cache is rebuilt whenever the panel is re-enabled.
- The panel's Station field is set by DemoToolsBuilder and saved with the scene, so OnEnable always sees it.
- The panel's own Remove button is deferred and runs at the end of the OnGUI event. ToolsChanged fires synchronously inside that call, so the cache changes at the same moment the hierarchy changes today. The next Layout and Repaint pair stays consistent.
- The order of the list is unchanged.
- The one place tools are destroyed without ToolsChanged is GlassToolValidation line 15 (DestroyImmediate). That is validator-only, OnGUI does not run in batch mode, and the `tool == null` skip covers it anyway.

Compiling and validators:
- It compiles on Unity 6000 with no packages. System.Collections.Generic is already imported and there is no member called `placed`.
- No validator reads the drawer lists. ShopCityValidation says outright that the panel never draws in batch mode, and the panel checks there and in DemoValidation and ShopRobberyDressing only use Layout, Contains, CapturesInput, ContextPrompt, RequestReset and Visible. Every check keeps passing.

Why the impact is only low:
- With 5 to 30 tools the cost is a walk over a few hundred transforms plus one array of a few hundred bytes, 2 to 4 times a frame. That is tens of microseconds.
- It only happens while the presenter has the drawer open on the Tools or Map tab.
- The same events already allocate several strings per row and per chip (DisplayName concatenation, the count and kind-name chips), so the drawer still allocates after this fix.

It is still worth doing because it is a tiny change that turns three walks of the same hierarchy into one.

confirmed.title: The default build ships the unbaked realtime preview, which is slower and looks worse
confirmed.problem: Start-Demo.cmd only passes -demoBake for `Start-Demo.cmd bake`. Both the default double-click and `rebuild` go through DemoBuild.BuildLatest (DemoBuild.cs:58/68), then NightStoreBuilder.BuildScene(bake:false) (NightStoreBuilder.cs:96-101), then NightLighting.UseRealtimeFallback (NightLighting.cs:427-449). Any later automatic rebuild after a git pull also falls back to the preview. The shipped scene then has 7 realtime lights: the moon as a realtime directional light, 4 streetlights, and 2 headlights forced to ForcePixel (line 438) whose 18 m, 55° cones cover most of the showroom and the pavement. Every object in those cones gets 2 extra ForwardAdd passes every frame for both eyes. Because the headlights are Important and pixelLightCount is 4, turning on the flashlight plus two scene lamps (Auto render mode, DemoLighting.cs:338-359, DemoToolGeometry.cs:178) pushes at least one lamp down to per-vertex or SH lighting. On the large merged Floor/Walls meshes, that lamp's light visibly disappears. The validator's realtime-light budget counts the fallback stand-ins separately (NightStoreValidation.RealtimeLights), so it never sees this. The preview also has no baked reflection-probe data, so glass and the floor reflect only the near-black procedural sky. It also has no headlight shadows, no bounce light, and a raised flat ambient. If a requested bake fails, BuildScene ignores the result and ships baked-only lights with no lightmaps, which renders black.
confirmed.fix: (1) Start-Demo.cmd:66-67: set `BAKEFLAG=-demoBake` by default and clear it only for `rebuild` (`if /i "%MODE%"=="rebuild" set "BAKEFLAG="`). Update the usage comments on lines 5-7. (2) NightStoreBuilder.BuildScene:96-101: `bool baked = bake && NightLighting.Bake(out string report); if (bake) Debug.Log(report); if (!baked) NightLighting.UseRealtimeFallback(root.transform);`, return `baked` and pass it to DemoBuild.WriteBuildInfo so the start menu reports the real lighting mode. (3) Set `light.renderMode = LightRenderMode.ForcePixel` in DemoLighting.Create (both torches) and in DemoToolGeometry.Lamp (after line 178). In UseRealtimeFallback (line 438), use LightRenderMode.Auto for the headlights. The handheld lights (at most 3 at once) then always keep a per-pixel slot within pixelLightCount 4. No validator checks renderMode or the launcher. RunNightQuick still runs the fallback, and 'Night quality settings applied' and the realtime-light-budget checks are unchanged.
confirmed.risk: Low for the code. Each new commit's first build takes several minutes longer (GPU lightmapper; much longer if it falls back to the CPU). In a preview build the headlights may be vertex-lit on objects that a torch and lamps already light.

votes.reason:
I tried to refute this and could not. The core claim holds on the real code path.

**The default build ships the preview.**
- Start-Demo.cmd:66-67 sets BAKEFLAG only when MODE is "bake". A plain double-click, `rebuild`, and every automatic rebuild after a pull changes the commit stamp all run without it.
- DemoBuild.BuildLatest:58 then calls BuildLatestReport(false), which calls NightStoreBuilder.BuildScene(false, false). BuildScene:101 calls NightLighting.UseRealtimeFallback.
- NightLighting's own comments call that fallback "A preview only, never the shipped look". HANDOFF line 48 describes the night store as "all baked".
- What the fallback does, confirmed in NightLighting.cs:427-449:
  - The moon becomes a realtime directional light.
  - The 2 near streetlights become realtime Auto and the 2 far ones ForceVertex.
  - The 2 headlights become realtime ForcePixel (Important), with an 18 m range and 55° cones aimed from the car at (0,1,2), so they cover a large part of the showroom.
  - No light keeps its shadows, and the ambient is raised to FallbackAmbient.
- The reflection probes are Baked mode, so with no bake they have no baked texture.

**The bake result is ignored.** BuildScene:96-100 throws away the bool that NightLighting.Bake returns. A failed bake therefore ships baked-only lights with no lightmaps, only the 0.015 flat ambient, and build info saying "baked".

**The handheld-light demotion is plausible.**
- Under Built-in forward rules, Important lights and the main directional light are always per-pixel. Auto lights only fill whatever is left of pixelLightCount 4, which NightQuality.PixelLights sets.
- In the fallback, the moon plus the 2 headlights use 3 slots, leaving 1 slot for the flashlight and up to 2 lit lamps (ToolStation.MaxLitLamps = 2; DemoLighting.Create and DemoToolGeometry.Lamp never set renderMode). On objects inside the headlight cones, at least one handheld light drops to vertex or SH lighting.
- In the baked build this cannot happen: at most 3 handheld lights are on at once, which fits in 4.

**The validator accepts the fallback.** NightStoreValidation.RealtimeLightChecks counts the fallback stand-ins separately and accepts them (arrivalFallback == stand). The finding's claim that it "never sees this" is accurate.

**Overstatements:**
- "Every frame for both eyes" is wrong for this build. The Start-Demo player is desktop only, with no XR plug-in (HANDOFF line 22; DemoLauncher.cs:9-10, 89). So the frame-cost part matters less than the realism loss.
- Only 2-3 of the 7 lights add ForwardAdd passes. The moon is drawn in the base pass, and the far streetlights are ForceVertex.

**The fix is safe.**
- No validator checks renderMode (grep finds only ShopInteriorFinish setting ForceVertex) or the launcher. RunNightQuick still calls UseRealtimeFallback directly.
- Making the handheld lights ForcePixel cannot reduce their quality in either mode.
- The main cost is build time. The night bake has never been run in Unity (there is no Docs/VerificationNight), so a default double-click would be the first real bake: minutes on the GPU lightmapper, possibly much longer on the CPU fallback.
- Part (2) of the fix, falling back to the preview when Bake returns false, removes the risk of shipping black lighting. Overall impact is medium-high: mainly realism, and performance on desktop.
votes.betterFix:
Apply all three parts, with these changes:
1. Make part (2) unconditional, even if the launcher default stays as it is. Fall back to the preview on any failure, not only a false return: if `LightmapSettings.lightmaps.Length == 0` after a successful-looking bake, call UseBaked and then UseRealtimeFallback too. Return the real mode and pass it to WriteBuildInfo, and also log it as `JEWELRY_BUILD_LIGHTING baked|preview` so the :fail filter and the console show it.
2. In the launcher, print a one-line notice before a baking build that it will take several minutes longer. Keep `rebuild` as the fast preview path.
3. Optional: skip the bake when only scripts outside NightStore*, NightLighting and StoreKit changed. Do this by keeping the previously baked scene when its hash matches, which avoids re-baking on every pull.
4. Update the 'Start-Demo.cmd' usage comments, HANDOFF line 20 and the NightLighting header comment to match. Do not describe the Start-Demo build as stereo or VR in any notes, because it is desktop only.

Rewrite the shader as a lit surface shader with the same name, properties and vertex deformation:
`Shader "CrimeScene/Tape" { Properties { _Color ("Yellow", Color) = (1,0.78,0.03,1) _Span ("Metres", Float) = 1 } SubShader { Tags { "RenderType"="Opaque" } CGPROGRAM #pragma surface surf Standard vertex:vert addshadow #pragma target 3.0 fixed4 _Color; float _Span; struct Input { float2 stripe; }; void vert(inout appdata_full v, out Input o) { UNITY_INITIALIZE_OUTPUT(Input,o); float h=v.vertex.y; v.vertex.y-=(1-4*v.vertex.z*v.vertex.z)*min(.035,_Span*.012)/.08; o.stripe=float2(v.vertex.z*_Span,h); } void surf(Input i, inout SurfaceOutputStandard o) { float band=abs(i.stripe.y)<.28?1:step(.28,frac(i.stripe.x*4+i.stripe.y*.25)); o.Albedo=lerp(fixed3(.025,.025,.018),_Color.rgb,band); o.Smoothness=0.45; } ENDCG } FallBack "Diffuse" }`

confirmed.problem: `directionalityMode = LightmapsMode.NonDirectional`, so the baked diffuse ignores the per-pixel normal. Almost all night lighting is baked, so the floor-tile, plaster, walnut, facade-stone and wet-asphalt normal maps only show inside the flashlight beam. GraphicsSettings use Forward (m_DefaultRenderingPath 1), so a camera with HDR on that renders into the LDR target from EvidenceCamera.cs:210 goes through an ARGBHalf intermediate and a resolve blit. When the camera has a target texture, Built-in takes the MSAA sample count from that RenderTexture. GetTemporary(width,height,24) has antiAliasing 1, so photos get no MSAA even though QualitySettings uses 4 (NightQuality.AntiAliasing=4, Ultra level AA 4, ShopPresentationExpansion sets 4). NightQuality.Configure only touches Camera.main. The 480x270 viewfinder also pays for the HDR intermediate and blit 15 times a second.

The fix compiles against Unity 6000 Built-in with no packages. The overload GetTemporary(int,int,int,RenderTextureFormat,RenderTextureReadWrite,int) exists, QualitySettings.antiAliasing is 0/2/4/8, so Mathf.Max(1,...) is valid, and Graphics.Blit from an MSAA RT with bindTextureMS=false resolves on its own.

The fix keeps every validator passing:
- Nothing checks the photo camera's allowHDR or MSAA. NightStoreValidation:559 checks Camera.main, and the photo camera is disabled and untagged.
- PanelChecks only asserts viewfinder width 480, photo.targetTexture==null and !photo.enabled. All three are unchanged.
- PhotoStage/ResetStage only check the file exists, PhotoCount, PhotoFrame.Current.width==1920, the camera pose and the review HTML. The capture flow, the pose restore and the 1920 width are unchanged, and no validator reads pixel content.
- Validators run in batchmode with a graphics device (no -nographics), so the MSAA render and blit execute as they do in a build.

Costs: about 75 MB of transient VRAM (4x colour and depth at 1080p, held in the temporary pool) and maybe 20-30% more GPU time for one camera render per photo. Both are small next to the synchronous ReadPixels stall already there. Turning HDR off also makes the 15 Hz viewfinder cheaper. With no post-processing, the visible difference from dropping HDR is limited to clamping order when glass is blended over values above 1, and it now matches the LDR night main view. It is worth doing: about 8 lines, and it visibly improves the photos, which are a deliverable of the demo (frame, panel, review.html).

Problems with the proposal as written:
- It names R4's async readback as part of the fix. It must not depend on R4. AsyncGPUReadback cannot read an MSAA RT, so if R4 lands the resolve is required, but without R4 the plain ReadPixels from the resolved RT works.
- The second temporary only needs depth 0, not 24.
- RenderTexture.active must be saved before Graphics.Blit, which changes it.
- Setting allowHDR in both the builder and Awake duplicates the same line. Awake alone covers new scenes, the regenerated night store and the older bundled JewelryStoreGlass scene.
- CLAUDE.md requires a validator check for the new behaviour, and the proposal adds none.

confirmed.problem: Render() draws the full lit scene from 20 m above, 4 times a second whenever the Full drawer is open. The clip drops KitGlass and the beacon column, which have no RenderType override. Add a `public Shader MapShader` field, assigned by DemoToolsBuilder so builds include it. In Render: `bool fog = RenderSettings.fog; RenderSettings.fog = false; if (MapShader != null) overview.RenderWithShader(MapShader, "RenderType"); else overview.Render(); RenderSettings.fog = fog;`.

- Exponential fog density is 0.01, so about 18% at 20 m (exp(-0.2) = 0.82).
- Every scene light is baked. The headlights give about 0.08 at the central cases, but they point roughly level, so the floor and the case tops, which are all the camera sees from above, get grazing light. The ceiling slab blocked the moon during the bake.

- The flashlight's spot shadow map is probably not rendered for this camera. NightQuality sets the shadow distance to 14 m and the floor is about 20 m from the camera.

- The validators only call Render() and check that the texture is not null or that the map's coordinate conversions are right (MapChecks, BackdropChecks, ShopRobberyDressing's ShouldRender checks). Nothing checks how the map is lit.

confirmed.title: Occluder flags are set but occlusion culling is never baked
confirmed.problem: MarkStatic sets OccluderStatic and OccludeeStatic on the walls, slabs and buildings. The builder even unflags the ceiling 'once occlusion is baked', and DemoOverviewMap and the validator's Overview capture turn occlusion off for the same reason. But nothing calls StaticOcclusionCulling.Compute, so every camera (main, viewfinder, photo) draws the whole exterior and showroom even from the office and side rooms.

The glass and facade frames are not occluders, so the street stays visible through the frontage.
confirmed.risk: Low. It adds 10-60 s to the build. The map and the cutaway capture already disable occlusion. The gain is modest, mainly behind the rear partition.

Its comment at lines 136-139 says the ceiling is unflagged "once occlusion is baked". confirmed.title: The street-facing backdrop is one 54 m probe-lit renderer, so it is lit uniformly
confirmed.problem: `across = new KitMesh { Lightmapped = false }` emits all five buildings across the street as one renderer with no uv2. MarkStatic therefore makes it probe-lit, and the whole 54 m × 13.5 m facade takes a single interpolated SH sample at its bounds centre, which sits inside the block and outside the probe hull. - StoreKit.MarkStatic(Buildings, false, true): the renderer is not small, so it gets ContributeGI and OccluderStatic. Lightmappable() is false, so receiveGI is LightProbes. NightLighting.LightmapScales skips it.
- With default BlendProbes and no anchor, Built-in takes one SH set at the bounds centre. That centre is about (1, 6.75, -21.9), inside building 3, which spans x -3.8..7.2 and z -27..-17. The last probe row is the far one at z = FarPavementZ + 1.5 = -15.5. The other probes are the interior grid and the near pavement and staging-bay grid. So the centre is about 6.4 m outside the hull, and the extrapolated sample comes from the far row near x 0..4, y 3..7.

- DressingChecks only needs BatchingStatic.

- CountUntouched only reports, and it scans StoreKit.Folder.

The only downside is a slightly longer bake.

confirmed.title: KayKit lightmap-UV margins are sized for a far higher texel density than the night bake gives them
confirmed.problem: OnPreprocessModel enables generateSecondaryUV but leaves the margin at the importer default. That is either Calculate at 40 texels per unit and object scale 1, or a Manual pack margin sized for a whole 1024 lightmap. In the night bake these models get far fewer texels per model unit: 10 (LightmapTexelsPerMetre) × 0.5 (KitScale) × 4.5 (ShopCityRefinement.KitScale) = 22.5 for the police car and streetlights, and 10 × 0.2 (FarScale) × 7 = 14 for the towers. The gaps between UV charts therefore come out at about one texel or less. On the KayKit car (many small charts, standing beside the spawn under the streetlights) and on the streetlights, that produces lightmap bleeding along chart borders: dark or bright seams and blotches. The postprocessor also has no GetVersion(), so changing its settings never reimports models that are already imported.
confirmed.fix: In OnPreprocessModel, alongside generateSecondaryUV = true, set `importer.secondaryUVMarginMethod = ModelImporterSecondaryUVMarginMethod.Calculate; importer.secondaryUVMinLightmapResolution = DemoGeometry.LightmapTexelsPerMetre; importer.secondaryUVMinObjectScale = 1;`. That is 10 texels per unit, below every placement's real density, so margins are always at least 2 texels. Add `public override uint GetVersion() => 2;` so Unity reimports the models once. In GenerateLightmapUVs, also treat a model as stale when `importer.secondaryUVMinLightmapResolution != DemoGeometry.LightmapTexelsPerMetre`.
confirmed.risk: Low. Wider margins slightly reduce packing efficiency on objects that occupy a few hundred texels. The GetVersion bump reimports every model in the project once (OBJs only).

votes.reason:
I could not refute it; the mechanism checks out in the code. ThirdPartyModelImport.OnPreprocessModel (line 17) only switches on generateSecondaryUV. There are no .meta files for the OBJs, in the repo or in the Glass zip, so the margin method, min lightmap resolution and min object scale are left at Unity's defaults: Calculate at 40 texels per unit and scale 1, or the legacy Manual margin of 4/1024.

The models are lightmapped in the night bake:
- StoreKit.MarkStatic(Exterior) sets ReceiveGI.Lightmaps on any renderer that is not small (0.3 m) and has uv2. That covers the car body, the wheels (0.65 m at scale 4.5), the streetlights and the towers.
- NightLighting.LightmapScales gives Exterior/PoliceCar and Exterior/Streetlights a scale of 0.5 (KitScale) and Exterior/Buildings 0.2 (FarScale).
- lightmapResolution is 10 (DemoGeometry.LightmapTexelsPerMetre).
- Model scales are 4.5 (ShopCityRefinement.KitScale) and 7 for the towers.

So the real density is 22.5 and 14 texels per model unit, against the 40 the default margins assume. Unity's own docs say a lower resolution than Min Lightmap Resolution can bleed. The project already fixed this for generated meshes (DemoGeometry.PrepareForLightmaps sizes the pack margin from the planned density, and its comment says the default margin bleeds), but not for imported models.

The car is at (4, -6.2), 2.5 m from PlayerSpawn (1.6, -5.4), so it is prominent. From the OBJ areas, the car's whole lightmap is about 34x34 texels, a streetlight about 8x8 and a wheel about 5x5. If the default is Manual, margins come out around 0.1 texel; under Calculate they are about 0.56x (car) and 0.35x (towers) of the intended size. Missing GetVersion() is also true: changing the settings will not reimport models that are already imported.

Problems with the finding's fix and risk statement:
1. "10 tpu is below every placement" is false for StoreKit override models. OverridePack "StoreKit" is under DemoAssetLibrary.Root and placed at scale 1: interior pieces get 0.8 x 10 = 8 texels per unit, the bollard 0.5 x 10 = 5. None ship today.
2. The risk is understated. With Calculate at 10 tpu and scale 1, a streetlight's minimum footprint is about 3.5 texels across and the car's about 15. Margins of 2 or more texels would take most of the UV space and shrink the charts to about one texel each, or hit whatever clamp Unity applies internally. It is not "slightly reduce packing efficiency on objects of a few hundred texels".
3. Settings changed in OnPreprocess may not be written back to the .meta. The stale check in GenerateLightmapUVs must set the properties before SaveAndReimport, or it will reimport on every build.

It is still safe to apply: it only affects uv2 generation, no validator checks margins, the daytime shop is not baked, and the one-time reimport only touches OBJs. Impact is real but closer to low-to-medium, since the car's lightmap resolution is coarse anyway.

Fix the density instead of only the margins. That is about 0.9 for the car and streetlights at 4.5, so the default Calculate margins are correct. The cost is a few thousand texels: the car becomes about 68x68 and each streetlight about 16x16.

Set the tiny parts (wheels, streetlight posts) and the far skyline towers to ReceiveGI.LightProbes but keep ContributeGI, so they still bake shadows onto the street. They then cannot bleed and save lightmap space.

If you prefer the importer route, set the margin per pack to the real placement rather than a blanket 10 at scale 1. For KayKitCity use Calculate with minLightmapResolution = LightmapTexelsPerMetre x NightLighting.KitScale (5) and minObjectScale = ShopCityRefinement.KitScale (4.5); the towers would need 2 and 7. Clamp the result the way DemoGeometry does. Bump GetVersion(), and in GenerateLightmapUVs write the settings before SaveAndReimport.

confirmed.problem: lightmapResolution = DemoGeometry.LightmapTexelsPerMetre = 10 (DemoGeometry.cs:135) gives 10 cm texels on the interior shell and 12.5 cm on fixtures (FixtureScale 0.8). - `directionalityMode = NonDirectional` is at line 394. Its only stated reason is the comment "non-directional lightmaps halve the memory". Git history and the docs give no other reason for 10 texels/m.

**The blur is a real problem.** The headlights are Baked, Soft shadows, with `shadowRadius 0.05`. The code comment says they are aimed so "the cases cast long shadows into the store". That asks for crisp penumbrae from thin case legs, which 10 cm texels cannot hold.

**The flat-normal claim holds for diffuse light.** Every textured palette surface is a Standard material with `_NORMALMAP` enabled (StoreKit.Surface plus DemoAssetLibrary.ApplyTextures). ReferenceTextures supplies normals for FloorTile, PlasterWarm, PavementSlab, AsphaltWet and the others. NightMaterials supplies normals for CeilingPaint and FacadeStone. With non-directional lightmaps, the Standard shader's baked diffuse ignores those normals. All scene lights are Baked, so the bump detail comes only from the realtime flashlight or lamp, and from specular in the baked reflection probes.

**Where the finding overstates:**
- Glossy surfaces such as the floor tiles still show their normals through the reflection probes, so "flat" is strictly true only for rough surfaces like plaster.
- CombinedDirectional stores one dominant direction per texel. Where the headlights and streetlights overlap, the normal response is only approximate.

**Budget looks fine but is unverified.** The interior footprint is 16x12 m (NightStoreLayout). A 0.2-0.5 Mtexel estimate for the current bake is plausible, since small props are probe-lit and not lightmapped. Four times that, plus direction maps, should stay well under LightmapBudget (8 maps of 1024). No run has confirmed this yet. NightStoreValidation.LightmapChecks prints the `Lightmaps=` line that would.

**Validators are unaffected.** None constrains resolution or directionality. The uv2 checks in StoreKitValidation and NightStoreValidation only test that UV2 is present and non-zero. The custom shaders have no lightmap variants, so DIRLIGHTMAP_COMBINED cannot break them.

**Scope of impact.** It applies only to the baked path: RunNight, `Start-Demo.cmd bake` and `-demoBake`. The default Start-Demo build uses the realtime preview. The baked look is still the intended shipped look, so the problem is real there. Raising the resolution costs nothing per frame. Directional maps cost one extra texture sample per lightmapped pixel plus a few MB, which is small on a PC-rendered Link target.

Raising the resolution costs nothing per frame (the sampling cost does not depend on resolution) and only about 0.5 MB per probe.

confirmed.title: Every photo stalls the main thread on a synchronous GPU readback and moves about 18 MB on the CPU
confirmed.problem: Capture() calls ReadPixels() (line 225) one frame after the 1920x1080 photo render. scratch.ReadPixels (287) is a synchronous GPU-to-CPU copy, so the main thread waits for the GPU to finish the frame still in flight, which includes both VR eyes and the photo render. scratch.Apply(false) (288) then uploads 6.2 MB back to the GPU, but that GPU copy is never used. GetRawTextureData() (289) allocates and copies another 6.2 MB managed array. On the PhotoSaved frame, LastPhoto.LoadRawTextureData plus Apply (257-258) uploads a third 6.2 MB. The comment at line 230 says the headset does not drop frames, but only the PNG encode is off the main thread.
confirmed.fix: Read the photo back asynchronously with UnityEngine.Rendering.AsyncGPUReadback, which is a built-in API and needs no package. After `rendered`, call `var req = AsyncGPUReadback.Request(target, 0, TextureFormat.RGBA32);`. Restore the camera (targetTexture, enabled, stereo, pose) right away as now, but keep `target` alive. Wait with `while(!req.done) yield return null;`. On `req.hasError` call Fail. Otherwise take `byte[] rgba = req.GetData<byte>().ToArray();` and release the RT. Inside the existing Task.Run, pack RGBA to RGB24 (one loop over 2 M pixels) before EncodeArrayToPNG(R8G8B8_UNorm), so the PNG and LastPhoto keep their current format and size. Split RestoreCamera so the RT is released only after the readback, and release it in Restore/OnDisable when the coroutine is stopped. Keep ReadPixels as a fallback when !SystemInfo.supportsAsyncGPUReadback, and delete scratch.Apply(false) in both paths. Optional: keep the RT until the save completes, then Graphics.CopyTexture it into LastPhoto instead of uploading again from the CPU.
confirmed.risk: Low to medium. The photo arrives 1-3 frames later. DemoValidation.PhotoStage already waits for !IsCapturing && LastPhotoPath != null, and 'Photo frame shows the saved photograph' only checks width 1920. The pose-restore check still passes because the pose is restored before the readback. Compare row order with the old ReadPixels output: check Docs/.../runtime-photo.png orientation after the first run.

- scratch.Apply(false) (line 288) uploads about 6.2 MB that nothing ever samples. A grep shows scratch is used only inside this file: it is created here, read back through GetRawTextureData, and destroyed in OnDestroy.

The problem is real, but the finding overstates it. In EvidenceCamera.Capture (Prototype/Scripts/EvidenceCamera.cs), ReadPixels() runs in the Update of the frame after the photo render. Texture2D.ReadPixels from an active RenderTexture is a blocking GPU-to-CPU copy. It makes the main thread wait for the render thread and then for the GPU to finish the previous frame, which includes both VR eyes and the 1920x1080 photo. scratch.Apply(false) (line 288) uploads a private texture that is never sampled, and on D3D11 RGB24 has no native format, so Unity also converts it to RGBA on upload. GetRawTextureData allocates another 6.2 MB on every shot, and the scratch texture keeps about 6 MB of CPU memory and 8 MB of GPU memory for the whole session. The comment at lines 230-232 is therefore wrong. However, this is a hitch of one to three frames per photo, not a per-frame cost, so 'high' is too strong; medium is closer. Even with the fix, the extra 2 MP camera render in that frame is a GPU spike that async readback does not remove.

Validators: DemoValidation.PhotoStage waits up to 30 s for !IsCapturing && LastPhotoPath != null. It checks only that the file exists, PhotoCount == 1, PhotoFrame.Current.width == 1920 and that the PhotoCamera local pose is restored. The pose is restored when the request is made, so all of these still pass. ShopCityValidation.PanelChecks (targetTexture == null, !enabled) and the NightStoreValidation reset checks are not affected. No validator scans the source for ReadPixels.

1. `while(!req.done) yield return null;` has no deadline. If a request never completes (for example a paused or odd batch-mode player loop, or device trouble), IsCapturing stays true for the whole session. That blocks every later photo and also freezes the viewfinder, because TickViewfinder returns early while IsCapturing is true. The existing render wait has a 10 s deadline for exactly this reason.
2. Requesting TextureFormat.RGBA32 is unclear in linear colour space. The temporary RT is R8G8B8A8_SRGB. If the requested format resolves to UNorm, Unity converts the data and the photo comes out darker. ReadPixels copies the bytes unchanged today.
3. The optional Graphics.CopyTexture into LastPhoto is wrong. An ARGB32 RenderTexture and an RGB24 Texture2D are not copy-compatible. Switching LastPhoto to RGBA32 would bring in the camera's alpha, which transparent and glass blending pushes below 1. The panel then draws the thumbnail with GUI.DrawTexture, which alpha-blends, so the thumbnail would look partly transparent.
4. Row order should match ReadPixels, because Unity renders into RenderTextures in the bottom-up OpenGL convention. No validator would catch a flip, though, so this stays unverified until someone looks at runtime-photo.png.

confirmed.title: A held tool trails the controller by one frame: Update order between HandInteractor and XRControllerInput is undefined
confirmed.problem: HandInteractor.Update positions the held tool from transform (FollowHand, line 27). XRControllerInput.Update on the same GameObject writes the new controller pose (XRControllerInput.cs 95-96). Neither has an execution order. DemoToolsBuilder.CreateHand adds HandInteractor (line 318) before XRControllerInput (321), so components enabled together will typically update in that order. FollowHand then uses the previous frame's hand pose, while the controller model and the camera body, which are children of the hand, use the new one. confirmed.fix: In XRControllerInput.Update, immediately after setting localPosition/localRotation (after line 96), add `if (hand.Held != null) hand.FollowHand();` so the tool follows this frame's pose whatever the order. confirmed.risk: Low. Without a device, XRControllerInput returns before touching the transform, so the validators, which set hand transforms directly and call FollowHand/Update, are unaffected. confirmed.title: Head and controller poses are read only in Update, never again before rendering
confirmed.problem: XRHeadTracking.Update and XRControllerInput.Update (93-96) read devicePosition/deviceRotation once per frame in Update. Unity's own TrackedPoseDriver defaults to UpdateAndBeforeRender because the XR input providers update poses again just before rendering with a shorter prediction horizon. Controllers, held tools and the flashlight (a child light) render with the Update-time pose.

confirmed.risk: Low. Interaction (grab, overlap, teleport validation) keeps using the Update pose. - The rebuild on fade is real but short. It rebuilds 22 TextMeshes per frame for about 0.2 s per fade, which is minor.

confirmed.title: Presenter map re-renders the whole store at 4 Hz while the drawer is open during a VR session

confirmed.title: The start-up recentre snaps the world without the comfort fade
confirmed.problem: DemoModeSwitch.RecentreNow calls XRLocomotion.Recentre once the head is tracked. Recentre rotates the rig by up to 180 degrees and moves it to the spawn in one frame, but unlike TryTeleport and SnapTurn it never calls ComfortFade.Fade(), so the visitor sees the world jump and turn when the headset starts tracking.
confirmed.fix: At the end of Recentre, add `if (ComfortFade != null) ComfortFade.Fade();`. Fade already returns when the fade component is disabled, which it is on the desktop.
